answer: Divergent challenge seeding assigns each identity a unique task whose answer must wander slightly from a shared prompt. Because clones running identical code produce identical outputs, the system flags any two identities that answer in lockstep, forcing a copy to fork behavior. Attackers must then write distinct per-identity logic, an opal-grade engineering cost that scales linearly with each fake account. Honest agents diverge freely like flowers in a meadow, while a sybil farm pays full development overhead for every node it fields.
